GroupDim.description:
One grouping dimension the `?group_by=` querystring accepts. Parsed case-insensitively from a
comma-separated list; unknown tokens are a client error (surfaced as `422` by the handler).

LeadTime.description:
Lead-time summary for the **closed** rows in a bucket, in whole seconds between `created_at` and
`closed_at`. `count` is how many closed rows had both timestamps parse (the sample size); the
stats are `None` when that sample is empty so the FE renders "n/a" rather than a misleading `0`.

count.description: Number of closed rows that contributed (both timestamps present + parseable).

max_secs.description: Maximum lead time in seconds; `None` when `count == 0`.

mean_secs.description: Mean lead time in seconds, rounded to the nearest second; `None` when `count == 0`.

median_secs.description: Median lead time in seconds; `None` when `count == 0`.

min_secs.description: Minimum lead time in seconds; `None` when `count == 0`.

StatBucket.description:
One aggregated bucket: the `key` names the group (one entry per requested dimension), and the
body carries the counts, progress, and lead-time roll-up over the rows that fell into it.

key.description:
The group key: `{ "<dim>": "<value>", ... }`, one entry per requested dimension in the
requested order. For `group_by=assignee,rig` this is `{"assignee":"alice","rig":"hq"}`.

lead_time.description: Lead-time summary over the bucket's closed rows.

other.description: Count of rows whose status is none of the above (defensive; usually 0).

progress_pct.description:
Progress as `closed / total * 100`, rounded to one decimal (0.0..=100.0). `0.0` when the
bucket is empty (cannot happen — empty buckets aren't emitted — but defined for safety).

total.description: Total rows in the bucket (`open + working + closed + other`).

StatsResponse.description:
The full statistics response: which dimensions were grouped on, the buckets, and a `totals`
roll-up across **all** rows (ungrouped) so the FE has a denominator without re-summing.

buckets.description: One bucket per distinct group key, sorted by key for a stable render order.

totals.description: Counts/progress/lead-time over every row, independent of grouping. Its `key` is empty.

200.description: Every agent session in the workspace

get.summary: `GET /` — every agent session in the workspace (`agent.list`).

422.description: A session with that id already exists

post.summary:
`POST /` — record a new agent session (`agent.spawn`). Emits `agent.spawned.v1`. A re-spawn of
an id already in the registry is a `422` (mirrors the MCP duplicate check). `201` on success.

get.summary: `GET /:id` — one session's state (`agent.info`); `404` when no session matches.

post.summary:
`POST /:id/end` — record a session's normal end (`agent.end`). Emits `agent.session-end.v1`,
folding the session to `done`. `404` on an unknown id.

`POST /:id/heartbeat` — record a liveness heartbeat (`agent.heartbeat`). Emits
`agent.heartbeat.v1`; a no-op on the registry but accepted + logged. `404` on an unknown id.

`POST /:id/kill` — record a session forcibly killed with a reason (`agent.kill`). Emits
`agent.killed.v1`, folding the session to `killed`. `404` on an unknown id; a missing `reason`
is a `422`.

200.description: Every convoy with its state + members

get.summary:
`GET /` — every convoy in the workspace with its state + members (`convoy.list`). Reuses the
replayed board so the projection matches the MCP read exactly.

200.description: Convoy launched; echoes the emitted event kinds

post.summary:
`POST /` — launch a convoy over an ordered member list (`convoy.launch`). The convoy id lives
in the body (it names the *new* resource, not an existing path), and dispatches the first
member. Emits convoy.created + convoy.launched + the first convoy.member-dispatched.

get.summary: `GET /:convoy` — one convoy's state + members (`convoy.info`); `404` when no convoy matches.

200.description: Member completed; echoes the emitted event kinds

422.description: Validation failed (not the active member / not launched)

post.summary:
`POST /:convoy/complete-member` — mark the active member done and hand off to the next, closing
the convoy when it was the last (`convoy.complete-member`). The convoy always comes from the
path and overwrites any `convoy` in the body (docs/03 Rule 6); the member is the body.

200.description: Member failed; echoes the emitted event kinds

422.description: Validation failed (not the active member / not launched)

post.summary:
`POST /:convoy/fail-member` — fail the active member and halt the convoy (`convoy.fail-member`).
The convoy comes from the path; `member` + `reason` are the body. Emits convoy.member-failed +
convoy.failed.

get.description:
Owner is optional: with both `owner_type`+`owner_id` it filters to one bead (back-compat);
with neither it browses the whole workspace. `content_type` narrows by MIME. The response is
the paged envelope `{ documents, offset, limit, has_more, next_offset }` (the `gt://issues`
shape) — `next_offset` is `null` on the last page.

200.description: A page of workspace documents (paged envelope)

get.summary:
`GET /?owner_type&owner_id&content_type&offset&limit` — a flat, paged browse of the
workspace's live documents, newest first (`documents.list.execute`, hq-web-extras.11).

500.description: No object store configured for a blob attach, or a store error

post.summary:
`POST /` — attach a document to a bead (`documents.attach.execute`). The id is minted
server-side (a ULID); `created_by` rides in the body (the agent's attribution, as on the MCP
path). `201` on success with the stored document.

get.summary:
`GET /search?query&owner_type&owner_id&limit` — hybrid (text + vector) search when an embedder
is wired, else phase-1 full-text (`documents.search.execute`). An embed failure degrades to
full-text rather than erroring, exactly as the MCP path does.

200.description: The workspace's shares with derived state

get.summary:
`GET /shares` — list the workspace's shares whose document is still live, with each share's
derived state (`active|expired|revoked`) computed now (`documents.read`).

delete.summary:
`DELETE /shares/:hash` — revoke a share (`documents.write`). Idempotent: a missing or
already-revoked share is still a `200`, so a double-DELETE is safe.

200.description: Share limit reset; returns the share

422.description: Validation failed (both forms set / bad timestamp)

patch.summary:
`PATCH /shares/:hash` — dynamically reset a share's limit: extend/shorten via `expires_in`
(seconds from now) or `expires_at` (RFC3339), or lift it entirely by sending neither
(`documents.write`). Returns the post-update share. `404` when the hash is unknown.

parameters.description: The version the caller last read
parameters.name: expected_version

delete.summary:
`DELETE /:id?expected_version` — soft-delete a document under its version guard
(`documents.remove.execute`). The id is the path; `expected_version` is the querystring (a
DELETE carries no body). `200` echoes the removed id.

get.summary:
`GET /:id` — one document with its body/extracted text + `version`; `404` when no live row
matches (`gt://doc/{id}` read).

patch.summary:
`PATCH /:id` — edit a document under its optimistic version guard (`documents.update.execute`).
The id always comes from the path and overwrites any `id` in the body (docs/03 Rule 6).
Returns the post-bump document so a follow-up edit can chain `expected_version`.

404.description: No live document with that id

post.summary:
`POST /:id/share` — mint a public capability URL onto a document (`documents.write`). The doc
id rides on the path. `expires_in` (seconds, optional) sets the TTL; omit it for no limit.
`201` with the share `{ hash, url, state, expires_at, ... }`. Several shares per document are
allowed, each with its own TTL.

parameters.description: 0-based page offset from the newest end (default 0)
parameters.name: offset

200.description: A page of the activity feed for the caller's workspace, newest-first

get.summary: `GET /?channel=&offset=&limit=` — a page of the caller's workspace activity feed, newest-first.

`GET /` — a paged snapshot of the tracker (`gt://issues`). Reuses
[`read_issues_page`](crate::resources::read_issues_page) so the page semantics match the MCP
resource exactly.

post.summary:
`POST /` — create a bead (`issues.create.execute`). The id lives in the body (it names the
new resource, not an existing path), uniqueness is enforced by the store. `201` on success.

get.description:
Returns counts `{open,working,closed,other,total}` + `progress_pct` (`closed/total`) +
`lead_time` (from `created_at`/`closed_at` on closed beads) for each bucket of the requested
`group_by` dimensions, plus an ungrouped `totals` roll-up. The aggregation runs over the
tracker rows of the active workspace (the same auth-scoped store the other handlers use —
tenant resolution is upstream, never a route param); the math itself lives in transport-free
[`crate::stats`]. Scope: `issues.read` (the GET verb-class the builder guards).

An unknown or empty `group_by` is a `422` (client error), matching the MCP parse path. The
rows are pulled with a high page limit (clamped by `GT_ISSUES_MAX_LIMIT`) so the aggregate
covers the whole workspace tracker in one pass.

200.description: Per-bucket counts + progress% + lead_time, plus ungrouped totals

get.summary: `GET /stats` — per-workspace aggregation for the statistics view (`gt-web.5`, `hq-web-extras.12`).

200.description: The issue with heavy bodies + version

get.summary:
`GET /:id` — one issue with its heavy bodies + `version` (`gt://issue/{id}`); `404` when no
row matches.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /:id` — patch editable fields (`issues.update.execute`). The id always comes from the
path and overwrites any `id` in the body (docs/03 Rule 6: identity is never trusted from the
payload). Returns the post-bump `version` so a follow-up edit can chain `expected_version`.

200.description: Claim won; echoes version + S5 fields

post.summary:
`POST /:id/claim` — atomically claim an open, unowned bead for the server actor
(`issues.claim.execute`). A lost claim is a `409 Conflict` naming the current holder, so the
caller cannot proceed as if it owns the bead; a win echoes the post-bump `version` and the
S5 prose/phase fields.

422.description: Validation failed (e.g. missing commit_sha for a code surface)

post.summary:
`POST /:id/close` — close the bead (`issues.close.execute`). The attribution actor is the
server identity in [`IssuesApiState`], never the body. A bead with a non-planned code
surface still requires `commit_sha` (delivered-code proof), enforced by the shared handler;
the git delivery verification (S2) is skipped on the REST path (see the module docs).

`POST /:id/transition` — move the status across the open/working/closed machine
(`issues.transition.execute`). Illegal moves are rejected by the store's status-guarded
update and surface as `422`.

200.description: Every slot on the workspace merge board

get.summary: `GET /` — every slot on the caller's merge board (`merge.list`).

422.description: Validation failed (empty fields or already submitted)

post.summary:
`POST /` — submit a bead's branch into the queue (`merge.submit`). The bead lives in the body
(it names the new slot, like the issues `create` / rig `add`); a duplicate submit is rejected
against the rehydrated board. `201` on success.

404.description: No merge slot for that bead

get.summary: `GET /:bead` — one bead's merge slot (`merge.info`); `404` when no slot matches.

404.description: No merge slot for that bead

post.summary:
`POST /:bead/complete` — the edge reports a landed merge, `Merging → Merged` (`merge.complete`).
The bead comes from the path; the landed `sha` lives in the body.

404.description: No merge slot for that bead

post.summary:
`POST /:bead/fail` — the edge reports a failed merge, `Merging → Failed` (`merge.fail`). The
bead comes from the path; the `reason` lives in the body.

404.description: No merge slot for that bead

post.summary:
`POST /:bead/start` — take a queued slot to the physical merge, `Ready → Merging`
(`merge.start`). The bead always comes from the path (docs/03 Rule 6).

200.description: The full tools/list (names, descriptions, input schemas)

get.summary:
`GET /help` — the server's `tools/list` payload (`meta.help.execute`): every
dispatchable tool with its description + input schema. A pure read, no state
change. The shape matches the MCP `meta.help` result exactly.

201.description: Gap bead minted; echoes { bead, operation, priority, external_ref }

post.summary:
`POST /report-gap` — surface a missing operation (`meta.report-gap.execute`):
the server mints a `hq-gap-<slug>-<ts>` bead so the gap enters the routine
catalog. The attribution actor is the server identity in [`MetaApiState`], never
the body. `201` on success, echoing the minted bead summary.

200.description: Every tracked account with its usage + window

get.summary:
`GET /` — every tracked account with its usage (`quota.list`). Reuses the replayed registry
so the projection matches the MCP read exactly.
`GET /:account` — one account's usage + window (`quota.info`); `404` when no account matches.

200.description: Window reconciled; echoes the emitted event kind

post.summary:
`POST /:account/probe` — reconcile the live window against provider remaining/reset
(`quota.probe`). The account comes from the path. Emits `quota.usage_probed.v1`.

200.description: Rotated; echoes the emitted event kind

post.summary:
`POST /:account/rotate` — rotate active usage off this account onto another (`quota.rotate`),
parking the source in cooldown. The path account is the `from_account` (the one rotated away
from, docs/03 Rule 6); `to_account` is the healthy target in the body. A rotation onto itself
is a `422`. Emits `quota.rotated.v1`.

200.description: Sample recorded; echoes the emitted event kind

post.summary:
`POST /:account/sample` — record a token-usage sample (`quota.sample`). The account always
comes from the path and overwrites any `account` in the body (docs/03 Rule 6); the rest of
the body (`session`/`model`/usage counters) is the sample. Emits `quota.tokens_sampled.v1`.

200.description: Every rig in the workspace catalog

get.summary: `GET /` — every rig in the caller's catalog (`rig.list`).

post.summary:
`POST /` — register a new rig (`rig.add`). The name lives in the body (it names the new
resource, like the issues `create`), uniqueness enforced by the catalog. `201` on success.

`POST /adopt` — adopt an existing on-disk rig into the catalog (`rig.adopt`). Same shape as
`POST /`; emits the distinct `rig.adopted` kind. `201` on success.

get.description:
A static segment, so it never shadows `GET /:name` (axum routes static before dynamic). `404`
when no rig in the workspace owns the prefix.

404.description: No rig owns that prefix in this workspace

get.summary: `GET /lookup?prefix=` — resolve the rig owning a given bead-id prefix (`rig.lookup-by-prefix`).
`GET /:name` — one rig's catalog entry (`rig.info`); `404` when no rig matches.

post.summary: `POST /:name/set-default-branch` — change a rig's default branch (`rig.set-default-branch`).

`POST /:name/set-prefix` — change a rig's bead-id prefix (`rig.set-prefix`). The name always
comes from the path and overwrites any `name` in the body (docs/03 Rule 6).

422.description: Validation failed (relative path, `..`, too long, or no-op)

post.summary: `POST /:name/set-worktree-root` — pin a rig's worktree-root override (`rig.set-worktree-root`).

200.description: Every registered skill + per-role bindings for the caller's workspace

get.summary:
`GET /` — every registered skill in the caller's workspace, in sorted order, with the per-role
bindings the dashboard hydrates from.

200.description: The skill + the roles that have it enabled

404.description: No skill registered under that id

get.summary: `GET /:id` — one skill by id (`404` when the workspace has no skill registered under that id).

`GET /` — every workspace in the catalog (`workspace.list`). A pure read straight
off the repository; the envelope matches the MCP tool's `{ "workspaces": [...] }`.

409.description: A workspace with that id already exists

post.summary:
`POST /` — provision a new active workspace in the catalog (`workspace.create`).
The id lives in the body (it names the new resource), uniqueness is enforced by
the decide layer (`409` on a duplicate). Runs the full [`WorkspaceActor`] cycle so
the change is a replayable event. `201` on success.

get.summary:
`GET /:id` — one workspace's id, name + status (`workspace.info`); `404` when the
catalog holds no such id.

post.summary:
`POST /:id/archive` — archive a workspace (`workspace.archive`, terminal). The
decide layer rejects an already-archived workspace as an illegal transition (`409`).

`POST /:id/resume` — restore a suspended workspace to active (`workspace.resume`).
The decide layer rejects a non-suspended source as an illegal transition (`409`).

`POST /:id/suspend` — reversibly disable an active workspace (`workspace.suspend`).
The decide layer rejects a non-active source as an illegal transition (`409`).

200.description: The live document behind an active share

404.description: Unknown / revoked share, or the document is gone

get.summary:
`GET /share/:hash` — PUBLIC, unauthenticated read of the LIVE document behind an *active*
share (hq-web-extras.9). Served outside the `/api/v1` auth chain. Lazy expiry: the state is
computed at read time. `active` ⇒ `200` with the document (markdown + metadata); `revoked` ⇒
`404`; `expired` ⇒ `410 Gone`; unknown hash / vanished doc ⇒ `404`. Never leaks session data.
